item.content:encoded:
I am still wondering what the old ENIAC style computers are for. I mean, giving the Universal Turing Machine nature of most computers including those, you can produce essentially 100.0% transparent emulations (down to the component level, even) of those early machines on a modern system without it breaking a sweat. And the Enigma-coders are, well… a generalised any kind of digital messaging encryption, really.

And, well, not every Protestant denomination is CoE/Anglican. Though they'd not be super popular in Italy, there are other orders that their chaplains could belong to.

(No Orthodox or Muslim, though? For the latter you'd more want Mecca and/or Medina of course…)

I do like the note about the E-class objects, by the way. It's a good way to mention that the SCPs aren't the only things the Foundation deals with, and indeed they're in some ways the unusual, more rare objects: their containment procedures are special, after all. For most anomalous items, you have a very simple, standard containment procedure: stick it in a box in the W warehouse vault 13 77 in the basement, along with tens or even hundreds of thousands of others, and forget about it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I quite like this, and I wasn't really gonna comment anything, but… gaaaaah! Tiny, tiny nitpicks that I cannot ignore! I'm so sorry:

Nitpick list
I spent way too much time on this
  • In the list list of contained SCPs, 649 comes before 643.
  • In the description for the office facilities:

consisting of a large, warehouse-like rooms

'a large' is singular, but 'rooms' is plural, which is it?

  • In the description for the gym:

various weights, bags and machines

There needs to be a comma after bags, because you're still listing things.

  • In the description for the range:

There are facilities allowing weapons to be shot by those who would not be permitted to take a weapon with them around the site.

While this isn't incorrect, saying 'would not' without giving the circumstance(s) isn't the best. It should either say 'are not', or give a circumstance like 'usually'.

  • In the description for the church:

The church is deceptively holy- although

Pretty sure you need another space between 'holy' and the '-', 'cause otherwise it looks like it was cut off with a dash rather than extended with a hyphen.

  • In the Notable Containment Incidents list, with the one for SCP-703:

however proper olfactory protocols were observed by Site-77 security ensured minimal losses during this breach.

This doesn't work, you can't have two past tense verbs for a subject without a connective. It should either say 'which ensured', 'and ensured', or 'ensuring'. Alternatively, you could take out the 'were', thereby making the security the subject for 'observed'. Also, there should be a comma after 'however'.

  • In the Notable Containment Incidents list, with the one for SCP-039:

and is known to have breached at least one SCP object, SCP-1957 which resulted in the creation of SCP-1837

There needs to be a comma after SCP-1957, because it's a side bit of information.

  • In the Notable Containment Incidents list, with the one for SCP-512:

deployed several helicopters to pursue them, before being recaptured D-512-33 was struck by a bolt of lightning

Considering that the section of the sentence after the comma is not a continuation of the information prior, it shouldn't continue straight on without a connective. It should have a 'but', 'however', or an alternative, or be a separate sentence. Admittedly, the current way it's written isn't completely grammatically incorrect, but it's not very good for describing the event effectively.

  • In the Additional Information:

She’d funnel them large sums money

Should say 'large sums of money'.

  • And finally, in the Additional Information:

Its current mission is holding anomalous phenomenon, researching its effects and maintaining normalcy/security in the region.

Here you're talking about phenomena in the singular. While it's not grammatically incorrect to explain how they're treating a plural of something in singular terms, it's not the best. It should really be: 'holding anomalous phenomena, researching their effects'. If you really want it to be singular, there should be an 'an' before 'anomalous' to indicate that. Also, there should be a comma after 'effects', because you're still listing things.

item.content:encoded:
Which type of noir are we talking about?
Neo and film both generally have protagonists who are detectives, whereas lit have protagonists who are victims, suspects or perps.

Protagonist
+ show block
– hide block

The narrator certainly doesn't come across as the victim or suspect. As for a detective or a perp, while foundation employees can easily be portrayed as any of the three, I'm just not getting enough of a vibe of who the narrator is supposed to be. I'm not saying there has to be a named narrator or an per-established character like in 88's but noir is protagonist focused and I'm not seeing enough to come up with a voice or an entity for the voice.

Stronger/more in depth metaphors or similes might help establish a voice that is more noir.

item.content:encoded:
You really need to collapse long posts like this as a courtesy to others.
That said:

I think you're missing a lot of the point of these. Each is intended to be a vignette capturing the vibe of the site, a sort of guided tour of the part of the lore it represents.

Site-77 is the heart of a fantastical noir world of atomic-powered superweapons, psychic spies, and plain-talking agents in trenchcoats and fedoras. Ergo, it is written as if one of these agents were describing it.

Site-88 is, much like the American South it is located in, a crossroads between the cutting edge modern world and things that remember days before barbed wire. Only fitting that the tour guide is one such thing.

Site-64 is a relatively young and unassuming site, efficient and laid back at the same time… but has risen to some minor importance recently. Hence, a modern and clinical document that doesn't spend a lot of time on details.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Is this page meant to be read/ was written in universe or out of universe?

+ show block
– hide block

The fact that it doesn’t break character and doesn’t acknowledge that this is an explanation for the purpose of writing entries leads me to believe it’s meant to be read as in universe, but as an in universe piece the tone feels out of place. It also brings up certain questions if its in universe like:

  • who wrote this?
  • Was it written by the Foundation or a GoI?

If this is written by the Foundation, why mention the “steel furniture that really digs into your ass”? If this is by the Foundation, why is it so nonclinical?

  • Who is written for?

Is this what the Foundation gives out to new employees? Is it what a GoI wants their sleeper cells to read?

Why does anyone in universe feel it necessary to put in foreboding remarks in site 77’s dossier like “Time will tell if this will have any noticeable effect.”? Hasn’t the Facility been around since the mid 1900’s? Shouldn’t it have been enough time to determine if it has had a noticeable effect?

  • How old is the site director Dr. Shirley Gillespie if she is indeed the woman in the photo? When was the photo taken? The phone looks like a 1907 magneto wall set that someone placed on a desk, and from what I can tell that’s at the latest around the 1930. Why would the Foundation hold onto outdated technology like that? If she was even as young 16 years old in as late as 1939 she would be 93 years old in 2016 and IIRC one of the listed SCPs is dated to around 2010. It seems hard to swallow that a person with as high of a stress job as running a secret non governmental organization wouldn’t be rendered unfit for work from the health complications of high stress occupations around their late 80s and again this 93 years old estimation is a generous estimation.
  • Why is has the anachronistic statement of “cutting-edge colour television” in the dossier? When was this written in universe if it was written in universe? Why has an outdated statement been left in? I realize that some of the SCPs listed as housed at site 77 are from the mid 1900s but some of them are also from the early 2000s, if the dossier is in universe and has been updated to list them, why haven the outdated statements been removed or adjusted?

Are the prior two misdirection? If so is then what good is it to the reader? As Scorpion451 and Sirens have mentioned there is potential benefit for the sake of worldbuilding but what good is worldbuilding if its based on either intentional inaccurate information or outdated information? I realize the Writing Guide page hangs the lampshade over that but as a reader how am I to tell if its outdated or fabricated?

On the subject of a “dossier” format wise this doesn’t read like a dossier. A dossier is “a collection of documents about a particular person, event, or subject” however the formatting doesn’t really come across as a collection of documents. While the horizontal lines sort of work as a topic change, it doesn’t scream different document. Overall the whole thing feels too cohesive and internally consistent by its own standard to be a collection of different documents.


Please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

Format wise this could be addressed by putting the topics into tabs not unlike what a dossier would look like; a quick google search and one will find that dossier brings up lots of pictures of folders and the site itself has the ability to have pages in this tabbed format, like the Secure Facilities Locations page or the Incident Reports, Eye Witness Interviews, and Personal Logs page.
As for the overabundance of internal consistency that could be addressed by having multiple authors write multiple sections of the dossier, but this goes beyond the scope of just this page.
To be completely honest the offhand portions kind of read like a travel brochure which I could certainly see having been written by at least one SCP, the number of which I cannot recall but it had something to do with a travel agency that let being who didn’t have the same senses as humans experience the earth, but this is a whole nother topic.
